vedic_reference.note: Sanjīvan is a Sanskrit name with deep roots in Hindu mythology and the Vedas. It is derived from the Sanskrit word 'sanjīvanam', which means 'the giver of life'. This name is mentioned in various Hindu scriptures and is often associated with the divine figure Sanjīvan, who is said to possess the power to grant immortality. The name is also used to refer to the act of preserving or reviving life, and is often used in the context of healing, rejuvenation, and longevity.
